User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the MUBAS Community Hub.

profileImageUrl.description: URL of the user's profile image.

reputation.description: The user's reputation score within the community.

Question.title: Question
Question.description: Represents a question posted in the community forum.

authorId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Question) The ID of the user who posted the question.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the question was created.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the question was last updated.

tagIds.description: References to Tag. (Relationship: Tag N:N Question) An array of tag IDs associated with the question.

Answer.title: Answer
Answer.description: Represents an answer to a question in the community forum.

authorId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Answer) The ID of the user who posted the answer.

questionId.description: Reference to Question. (Relationship: Question 1:N Answer) The ID of the question this answer belongs to.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the answer was created.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the answer was last updated.

isAccepted.description: Indicates whether this answer has been accepted as the best answer to the question.

KnowledgeBaseArticle.title: KnowledgeBaseArticle
KnowledgeBaseArticle.description: Represents an article in the knowledge base.

id.description: Unique identifier for the knowledge base article.

title.description: The title of the knowledge base article.

content.description: The content of the knowledge base article.

authorId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N KnowledgeBaseArticle) The ID of the user who created the article (typically an admin).

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the article was created.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the article was last updated.

category.description: The category of the knowledge base article (e.g., Wi-Fi, SMIS).

tagIds.description: References to Tag. (Relationship: Tag N:N KnowledgeBaseArticle) An array of tag IDs associated with the article.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a tag that can be associated with questions or knowledge base articles.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Represents a notification for a user.

userId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Notification) The ID of the user who the notification is for.

type.description: The type of notification (e.g., new answer, question update).

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the notification was created.

isRead.description: Indicates whether the notification has been read by the user.

relatedItemId.description: The ID of the item related to the notification (e.g., question ID, answer ID).

relatedItemType.description: The type of item related to the notification (e.g., question, answer).

LiveUpdate.title: Live Update
LiveUpdate.description: Represents a live update or announcement.

id.description: Unique identifier for the live update.

content.description: The main content of the update.

category.description: Category of the update (e.g., Announcement, Maintenance).

authorId.description: The ID of the admin user who posted the update.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the update was created.

relatedArticleId.description: Optional ID of a related knowledge base article.

admin.description: Grants administrative privileges across the application.

params.name: questionId
params.description: The unique identifier of the question.

params.name: questionId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent question.

params.name: answerId
params.description: The unique identifier of the answer.

definition.description: Stores knowledge base articles. Only admins can create, update, or delete articles. Everyone can read.

params.name: articleId
params.description: The unique identifier of the knowledge base article.

definition.description: Stores live updates and announcements. Only admins can create updates. Everyone can read.

params.name: updateId
params.description: The unique identifier of the live update.

definition.description: Stores tags that can be associated with questions or knowledge base articles.  Tags can be read by anyone, but only admins can create, update, or delete them.

params.name: tagId
params.description: The unique identifier of the tag.

definition.description: Stores notifications for a specific user. Only the user and admins can access these notifications.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user.

params.name: notificationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the notification.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure security, scalability, and ease of debugging, following the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization of authorization data (e.g., user roles) directly into documents where access control is required, avoiding costly and complex `get()` calls in security rules. Structural Segregation ensures each collection has a homogeneous security posture. Access Modeling employs path-based ownership for private user data and membership maps for collaborative data. Data Clarity and Predictability are maintained through explicit state modeling and consistent naming conventions.

Specifically, the `/users/{userId}` collection stores user profiles. The `/questions/{questionId}` collection stores community forum questions, with denormalized `authorId` for simpler rule creation related to ownership. The `/answers/{answerId}` subcollection nested under `/questions/{questionId}` stores answers to specific questions, ensuring a clear hierarchical relationship. The `/knowledge_base_articles/{articleId}` collection stores articles, and the `/tags/{tagId}` collection stores tags. Notifications are stored under `/users/{userId}/notifications/{notificationId}`, providing a direct and easily secured path for user-specific notifications. Roles are managed in a dedicated `/roles_admin/{uid}` collection.

This structure facilitates simple and robust security rules. For example, a rule can easily check if `request.auth.uid == resource.data.authorId` to allow a user to update their own question. List operations are secured by ensuring that collections only contain documents that the user is authorized to access. Roles are determined by the existence of a document in a specific role collection (e.g., `/roles_admin/{uid}`), not by custom claims, adhering to the DBAC principle. The consistent use of naming conventions and explicit data modeling enhances debuggability.
